items.title: A New Lethal Front in Ukraine: Its Beloved Gas Stations
items.summary: Russian drone attacks have hit hundreds of gas stations in apparent retaliation for Ukraine’s attacks on oil refineries.

items.title: Andy Burnham’s First Weeks as UK Prime Minister: TikToks, Podcasts and Promises
items.summary: Andy Burnham’s whirlwind of TikToks, podcasts and promises appears to be resonating with some voters. But he faces big decisions about how to pay for it all.

items.title: Pakistan’s Kashmir Problem
items.summary: A wave of protests is posing the most significant challenge in years to Islamabad’s authority in the region.

items.title: Airport chaos, delays as E.U. debuts biometric border system
items.summary: The biometric system for non-E.U. citizens is causing long delays and short tempers at airports. Officials say the rocky rollout will get better and will improve security.

items.title: New Zealand Has Ended Greyhound Racing. Now It Has to Manage the Aftermath.
items.summary: As the country holds its final greyhound race, the government has committed to finding homes for dogs and supporting people whose livelihoods depended on racing.

items.title: More Than 170 Migrants Rescued From Burning Boat in English Channel
items.summary: No deaths or injuries were reported. Many migrants try to reach Britain in small, often unseaworthy vessels.

items.title: Ceuta Migration Crisis Exposes Despair Among Morocco’s Young People
items.summary: Moroccan migrants described their despair at their economic future, explaining what propelled them across the border with Spain.

items.title: Iran Says No Current Talks With U.S. After Trump Cites Progress on the Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: President Trump cited progress in the negotiations when canceling a threatened attack on Iran over the weekend. Iran said there were no current talks with the United States.

items.title: After Trump Pardon, Former Honduras President Hernández Faces Charges in His Home Country
items.summary: Juan Orlando Hernández, the former leader, faces fraud and money laundering charges after a Trump pardon overturned a drug-trafficking sentence.

items.title: As France’s Elders Swelter in the Heat, Postal Workers Come to the Rescue
items.summary: To help prevent heat-related deaths, the French government has asked postal workers to check in on older people.

items.title: Appeals Court Says E.P.A. Cannot Block Billions in Climate Grants
items.summary: The funds have been frozen since early in President Trump’s second term.

items.title: Judge Sets Paramount-Warner Bros. Merger Trial for March

items.title: SpaceX, in First Earnings After IPO, Reports Soaring AI Spending
items.summary: Elon Musk’s rocket company said its capital expenditures jumped nearly seven times from a year ago. Revenue also rose.

items.title: Justice Dept. Charges Doctor in $95 Million Skin Substitute Fraud Scheme
items.summary: Dr. Stephen Dubin, a wound care doctor in Nevada, is accused of applying unneeded, expensive wound coverings to seniors. He used the profits to buy yachts, the department said.

items.title: S&P 500 Hits Record High as Stock Market Worries About Iran and AI Ease
items.summary: The S&P 500 rose 1.8 percent, pushing past its previous peak at the start of June and capping a big turnaround from a recent sell off in technology stocks.

items.title: Man’s Claim That Brakes Failed on Jaguar Was Scam to Avoid Car Payments, Court Rules
items.summary: Nathan Owen called the police, saying he was trapped in a runaway car. A judge determined it was a lie and sentenced him to more than four years in prison.

items.title: Medicaid Urges States to Increase Autism Therapy Oversight
items.summary: The program’s spending on the therapy has quintupled since 2021, far outstripping the growth in diagnoses and raising concerns about overprescribing and fraud.

items.title: Warsh Wanted ‘Regime Change.’ A Reset Might Need to Come First.
items.summary: After his latest appearance set off a bout of volatility, Kevin M. Warsh, the chairman of the Federal Reserve, is under pressure to clear up mixed signals about his commitment to getting inflation down.

items.title: U.S. Trade Deficit Dips in June Along With ‘World Cup Effect’
items.summary: Imports and exports both declined, retreating from a busy month in May, data from the Commerce Department showed.

items.title: Why Wall Street Is Feeling So Bullish
items.summary: Booming corporate profits are driving the S&P 500 near another record, dampening concerns about the war, inflation and more.

items.title: In Lawsuit, NJ Accuses Amazon of Suppressing Pay for Delivery Drivers

items.summary: The voluntary review process will cover closed-source artificial intelligence models, but exclude those that publish the underlying code.

items.title: A SpaceX Rocket Will Soon Crash Into the Moon
